gen_risks.description: Weak procurement capacity at ADISA may cause delays, non‑compliance, and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire qualified procurement specialist, provide bank technical assistance, use sample TORs, and enforce close bank oversight of procurement processes.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risk rating is High. Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency. (Section 66)

gen_risks.description: Overall financial management risk is substantial due to limited experience of ADISA and MIPA with large donor‑funded operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver targeted fiduciary training, adopt a detailed Financial Management Manual, hire finance specialists, and implement robust internal controls with bank supervision.
gen_risks.evidence: Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial. ADISA and MIPA lack experience with large donor‑funded operations. (Section 62)

gen_risks.description: Ambitious timeline for constructing the central Citizen Service Center may be missed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a realistic construction schedule with contingency buffers, monitor milestones regularly, consider PPP financing options, and secure timely approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: Central CSC building to be constructed in Tirana by first half of 2017; timeline described as very ambitious. (Section 7)

gen_risks.description: Lack of existing IT systems and fragmented registers hinder integration and achievement of Level 3 automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a phased IT implementation plan, allocate resources for system development, enforce interoperability standards, pilot test services, and coordinate with NAIS for integration.
gen_risks.evidence: Seven institutions have no IT system; legacy registers are paper; integration required for Level 3 automation. (Section 10)

gen_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance from ministries and staff may impede front‑office reforms and service redesign.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a change‑management program, involve staff in redesign, provide training on new processes, communicate benefits, and create incentives for adoption.
gen_risks.evidence: Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back‑office functions; ministries may not welcome ceding front‑office function. (Section 58)

gen_risks.description: Delay in passing omnibus legislation needed for regulatory reforms could stall service re‑engineering.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate legislative drafting, set clear parliamentary timelines, engage legal experts, monitor progress, and prepare contingency measures for partial implementation.
gen_risks.evidence: Reform of government services will be implemented through omnibus legislation expected to be passed by end of 2016. (Section 19)

gen_risks.description: Construction of the CSC may cause dust, noise, waste and other environmental impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, conduct regular site inspections, and maintain a community liaison for grievance handling.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential environmental impacts of new CSC construction include dust, noise, waste; mitigated by EMP. (Section 70)

gen_risks.description: Emphasis on digital services could marginalize poor and vulnerable citizens with low internet access.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain non‑digital service points, provide assisted internet access, run targeted outreach campaigns, and ensure information is available via posters, call centres, and community centres.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art online services may diminish access of the poor and vulnerable due to low internet penetration. (Section 6)

gen_risks.description: Delay in recruiting procurement and administrative specialists for the PMU may weaken project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track recruitment, use interim consultants if needed, define clear TORs, and obtain bank assistance for procurement support.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement and Administrative Specialist positions have been readvertised; PMU staff not yet fully set up. (Section 66)

gen_risks.description: Results‑Based Financing disbursements are blocked until DLI#5 (strategic plan approval and baseline survey) is achieved.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize completion of the strategic plan and baseline survey, allocate dedicated resources, and provide technical assistance to meet DLI#5 on schedule.
gen_risks.evidence: No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved. (Section 31)

gen_risks.description: Complex coordination among multiple ministries, agencies, and inter‑ministerial committees may cause delays and misalignment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear coordination mechanisms, regular steering‑committee meetings, assign a dedicated coordination officer, and use project‑management tools to track responsibilities.
gen_risks.evidence: Multiple inter‑ministerial committees and working groups; coordination among many agencies is required and may be complex. (Section 58)

gen_risks.description: ADISA, as a newly created agency, has limited implementation experience and capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide intensive capacity‑building, hire experienced managers, leverage technical assistance, and monitor performance against clear milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: ADISA created in Oct 2014; limited track record; capacity strengthening needed. (Section 41)

gen_risks.description: Improved service access may increase demand, creating budget pressures amid existing fiscal constraints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct demand forecasting, adjust budget allocations, explore additional financing sources, and implement cost‑recovery where appropriate.
gen_risks.evidence: Improved access may increase demand for services, with budget implications; fiscal constraints noted. (Section 49)

gen_risks.description: High levels of perceived corruption may persist, undermining public trust in the reform outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen anti‑corruption controls, enforce front‑office separation, monitor bribery reports via citizen feedback, and run public awareness campaigns.
gen_risks.evidence: Corruption remains high; 30% of citizens exposed to bribery; risk reforms may not fully reduce it. (Sections 1‑3)

gen_risks.description: Low response rate (≈22%) to the citizen feedback mechanism may limit data quality for performance monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Increase outreach, diversify feedback channels, offer incentives for participation, and supplement with periodic surveys to improve data completeness.
gen_risks.evidence: Citizen feedback mechanism response rate about 22%; limited data may affect performance monitoring. (Sections 40‑41)

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
